Total Sleep Time = sleepperiod - self-reported WASO. Primary outcome. NA when self-reported WASO is missing or untrusted; use sleepperiod_minutes as an upper bound in that case.
Sleep Onset Latency computed from timestamps (time_sleep - time_bed). Pairs with sol_selfreport_minutes.
Sleep efficiency on a 0-100 scale = TST / trysleep * 100
Time in Bed = getup - bedtime. Contains SOL  sleep  WASO and post-awakening time.

Sleep period = awakening - sleep onset. Identical BY CONSTRUCTION to the former trysleep_minutes because this diary records no mid-sleep awakening timestamps. Also serves as the upper bound of TST when WASO is unavailable.

WASO under this study's operational definition = getup - final awakening. Source column is in HOURS; multiplied by 60 here so it is directly comparable with waso_selfreport_minutes. NOT a substitute for waso_selfreport_minutes: on real data (n=1723 paired) the two have near-identical marginal distributions (both median 10 min; both Q3 20 min) but night-level correlation is r=0.013. Use them as two variables not as two measurements of one quantity.
Mean duration per awakening bout = self-reported WASO / self-reported bout count. BOTH numerator and denominator are self-reported.
Participant's own SOL estimate. Pairs with sol_computed_minutes for discrepancy analysis.
Participant's own total WASO estimate. Pairs with waso_computed_minutes but does not track it night to night (r=0.013). Values are heavily rounded to multiples of 5 which attenuates any correlation.

Which algorithmic rule was applied (e.g. sleep_reduce_12h_loop). Belongs in B so that 'how much it moved' and 'which rule moved it' live in one table. CAVEAT: records only the ALGORITHMIC action and is never rewritten when a later manual correction overrides it.
